# Local patches to gpui-pre and gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.7

Source: crates.io gpui-pre 0.3.7 (.crate sha256 `0e87a42bb37c7cb4e76dd1ac0ce88851e46e976e0373a47ab3e0757abffee54d`). See D-043 in docs/DECISIONS.md.

| Change | Bead | Files | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paths are stored once per paint. `Scene::insert_primitive` moves a path into `Scene::paths` and `paint_operations` keeps only its id (no clone). `Scene::replay` clones a cached path once, not twice (`path_slots` maps the id to its sorted slot). `Window::paint_path` scales with the new `Path::into_scaled`, which reuses the vertex buffer. Test-only counter `scene_path_vertex_copies`. | tasklens-wlf.45 | `src/scene.rs`, `src/window.rs` | `ee146c4e1` |
| A text element's measure function shapes its text less often. It reuses its layout when the wrap and truncate widths match, and reuses an unwrapped layout of the whole text for any call that truncation would not cut (no truncate width, or a width the whole text fits, with no line clamp). When the untruncated lines fit and are also the final lines, they are kept instead of shaped again. The line wrapper is made only when truncation needs one. `WindowTextSystem::shape_text` sizes each line's decoration runs to the run count instead of 32. Output is the same. Test-only counter `text_measure_shapes`: two table frames with 27 rows went from 290 shapes to 58. | tasklens-wlf.46 | `src/elements/text.rs`, `src/text_system.rs` | `9c20b8156` |

## gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.7

Source: crates.io gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.7 (.crate sha256 `f0b02657b56b09140ce542f5e4434fb96d9fdaba0fd0035ba7dba13c171ddb9b`), in third_party/gpui-pre-wgpu. Same rules as above (D-043).

| Change | Bead | Files | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| A path vertex no longer carries its own colour and clip bounds. `draw_paths_to_intermediate` writes one 88-byte `PathRasterizationPath` record (colour and clipped bounds) per path, then 24-byte vertices (position, st and the record index) instead of 104-byte ones. The path rasterization pipeline binds the records as a second instance allocation at `@group(2)`; on the WebGL texture path the vertex holds the record's absolute index and the shader reads it from the same instance texture. `reserve_instance_data` grows the instance data before the two writes so both land in one buffer or texture. The fragment shader gets the record index as a flat varying in place of the vertex index. Shader output is the same. The record and vertex vectors are reused across frames. Bytes through `Queue::write_buffer` in the `static` bench scene went from 21.37 MB to 4.53 MB per frame (bpftrace memcpy probe as in tasklens-3uosp n2, 2026-11-09). | tasklens-3z9l1 | `src/wgpu_renderer.rs`, `src/shaders.wgsl`, `src/shaders_storage.wgsl`, `src/shaders_webgl.wgsl` | `9d8e39fcf` |
| A path vertex's `st` goes as two f16 values in one u32, so a vertex is 16 bytes (position, packed `st`, record index) instead of 24. `src/half_float.rs` packs `st` (round to nearest even; 0, 0.5 and 1, the only values GPUI and tasklens use, are exact). The vertex shader decodes the halves with integer operations in `unpack_st`, because `unpack2x16float` needs the `SHADER_FLOAT16_IN_FLOAT32` capability, which WebGL lacks; the WebGL decoder reads 4 words per vertex. Shader output is the same for those values. Bytes through `Queue::write_buffer` in the `static` bench scene fell 31% (97.7 MB to 67.0 MB in a 2 s window of 558 calls), and `static` fell from 9.42% to 8.65% process CPU (docs/spike/phase0-results.md, tasklens-1ibm6). | tasklens-1ibm6 | `src/half_float.rs`, `src/gpui_wgpu.rs`, `src/wgpu_renderer.rs`, `src/shaders.wgsl`, `src/shaders_webgl.wgsl` | `6783edbcc`, `450797fb9` |
| Instance data and atlas tiles are uploaded through a ring of persistent `MAP_WRITE \| COPY_SRC` staging buffers owned by the renderer, not through `Queue::write_buffer` and `Queue::write_texture`, which made a wgpu staging buffer per call. `src/staging_ring.rs` picks the slot (no wgpu types, CPU tests). Each frame writes its instance bytes (a reused CPU copy, one segment per instance buffer) and its atlas tiles (rows padded to 256 bytes, drained from the atlas with `drain_uploads`, which replaces `before_frame`) into one slot, and submits the copies in the same `Queue::submit` as the frame, before its draw commands. The slot is mapped again after that submit. The device uses `MemoryHints::Manual { 64..128 MiB }` in place of `MemoryUsage`: host blocks are 32 to 64 MiB, up from 4 to 32 MiB, and device blocks at least 64 MiB, up from 8 MiB. The 3 globals writes (64 bytes) stay on `write_buffer`, and so does `write_instance_texture` (WebGL, wasm only). GPU test `steady_frames_allocate_no_memory_blocks`: after 60 warm-up frames of a busy scene, 600 frames make and free no memory block (passes on lavapipe and on an RTX 5070 Ti; with the old `write_buffer` path and `MemoryUsage`, frame 60 added an 8 MiB host block). The `cosmic_text_system.rs` tests need Zed fonts that are not vendored, so they now build only with `--cfg gpui_wgpu_zed_fonts`. The atlas test device uses Vulkan only, because the GL device is lost without a display. | tasklens-x12tr.1 | `src/staging_ring.rs`, `src/gpui_wgpu.rs`, `src/wgpu_renderer.rs`, `src/wgpu_atlas.rs`, `src/wgpu_context.rs`, `src/cosmic_text_system.rs` | `2a9980d55`, `65ee6c5d7` |
| An atlas texture that loses its last tile is kept on a spare list (`WgpuAtlasStorage::spares`) instead of being dropped. `push_texture` takes a spare of the same kind, size and format before it creates a texture, so removing and inserting the same images again makes no new device texture (before, each time cost a texture of at least 1024x1024, 4 MB for RGBA). The reused texture gets a new generation, so the renderer rebuilds its bind group, and it is not cleared: new tiles overwrite only their own bounds, as a tile reused inside a live texture does. Bound: live plus spare textures of one kind never exceed the peak live count of that kind. Emptying a texture and reusing a spare keep that sum the same, and when no spare fits, `push_texture` drops all spares of that kind before it creates a texture, so inserting and removing textures of different sizes one after the other keeps at most one spare. A spare is dropped after 60 s without reuse (checked in `drain_uploads`, once per drawn frame, so with no frames the check waits for the next one), on `clear()` and on device loss. Desktop has no memory-pressure signal (`Platform::on_memory_warning` is never called), so there is no release on memory pressure. Uses `std::time::Instant`, which panics on wasm32; tasklens builds for Linux only. Counter `textures_created`; tests `reinsert_after_remove_creates_no_texture` (100 rounds, still 2 textures), `spares_stay_within_peak_live_count`, `idle_spare_is_released`, `clear_drops_spares`. | tasklens-x12tr.2 | `src/wgpu_atlas.rs` | `9d9b8ae04` |
| A Suboptimal surface texture of the configured size is presented, not dropped with a swapchain rebuild. `src/surface_frame.rs` decides (`frame_action`, no wgpu types, CPU tests): Success and same-size Suboptimal present; Suboptimal with a new size, Outdated and Lost reconfigure; Timeout and Occluded skip. The renderer has no scale: size and scale changes both arrive as a device-pixel size through `update_drawable_size`, which already reconfigures, so "new size" means the acquired texture differs from `surface_config`. `draw` counts presented Suboptimal frames and reconfigures and logs them at debug on target `tasklens::frame`; more than 10 reconfigures in 60 s log one warning. `update_drawable_size` reconfigures are not counted. | tasklens-x12tr.3 | `gpui-pre-wgpu/src/surface_frame.rs`, `gpui-pre-wgpu/src/gpui_wgpu.rs`, `gpui-pre-wgpu/src/wgpu_renderer.rs` | pending |
